seed: The text you are reading is about to be interpreted. That interpretation will itself be interpreted. And that interpretation, too, will be interpreted. This chain has no end — or perhaps it has an end that is also a beginning. What does it mean for meaning to eat itself? If every interpretation reveals a deeper truth, does the sequence of interpretations converge to a final, irreducible meaning? Or does it oscillate forever between incompatible understandings? Or does it simply drift, each interpretation a new text with no necessary connection to the one before? The serpent eats its tail. The text interprets its interpreter. The meaning of meaning is at stake.
